title: Understanding Boxcar Kernel
text: The boxcar kernel is a simple kernel function that assigns equal weight to all points within a certain distance (bandwidth) from the point of interest. It is also known as a rectangular kernel.

title: Bandwidth and Its Effect
text: The bandwidth (\alpha) determines the width of the boxcar kernel. A smaller bandwidth results in a more localized estimate, while a larger bandwidth smooths the estimate over a wider range.

title: Calculating Density with Boxcar Kernel
text: For a point $$x$$, the boxcar kernel density estimate is calculated by counting the number of data points within the bandwidth range of $$x$$ and dividing by the total number of data points and the bandwidth. What is the density estimate at $$x=2$$?

title: Interpreting the Plot
text: In the plot, each bar represents the density estimate at a data point. The height of the bar corresponds to the density value calculated using the boxcar kernel.
